chunks: 35. My father (RA) narrated it, saying: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Salmah al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (AS)

He said: Whenever there is food in the town other than what one person has bought, it is permissible for him to seek the surplus with his commodity, because if there is food in the town sufficient for the people, the price will not rise because of him; rather, it rises only if one person buys all that enters the city.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for permissible price increase or hoarding in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that individual profit-seeking is permissible provided the market supply remains sufficient for the general populace, distinguishing this from 'gharar' (excessive uncertainty/manipulation) caused by monopoly. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that price fluctuations are natural market dynamics rather than divine intervention, unless a single agent hoards the entire city's supply to artificially inflate costs. The narration underscores the importance of market liquidity and the prohibition of monopolistic practices that harm the community's economic stability.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 35. My father (RA) said with it that Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said, on the authority of Ya`qub ibn Yazid, on the authority of Safwan ibn Yahya, on the authority of Salmah al-Hannat, that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:

Whenever there is food in a town other than what one person has bought then it is permissible for him to hold on to the excess of commodity. If there is sufficient food available for people in the city, then the price will not rise merely because one person purchases the excess. Verily, the price only rises if one person buys all the food that enters the city.
